differences: Yellow staining when bruised, especially near base.
Strong phenol-like chemical odor.
Cap becomes flat earlier in growth.

safe_mushroom.name: Amanita caesarea
safe_mushroom.description: Highly prized edible Amanita with orange cap and white gills.

differences: Death cap has greenish to olive cap, not orange.
White gills and stem may look similar, but lacks striations.
Toxic even in small quantities; no safe preparation.

safe_mushroom.name: Boletus edulis
safe_mushroom.description: Popular porcini, thick white stalk, no color change.

lookalike.name: Rubroboletus satanas
lookalike.description: Toxic bolete, red pores, blue staining flesh.

differences: Devil's bolete bruises blue when cut.
Red pores and stem distinguish it from B. edulis.
Unpleasant smell compared to nutty aroma of B. edulis.

safe_mushroom.name: Cortinarius caperatus
safe_mushroom.description: Known as 'Gypsy mushroom', edible with wrinkled cap.

differences: Orellanus has brighter orange-brown cap.
Gills may remain more rust-colored than grey.
Toxicity not removed by cooking.

safe_mushroom.name: Entoloma saepium
safe_mushroom.description: Mild, edible species found near hedges.

lookalike.name: Entoloma sinuatum
lookalike.description: Deadly Entoloma, white gills and foul smell.

differences: Sinuatum has white gills that turn yellowish.
Larger size and more bulbous base.
Causes gastrointestinal distress within hours.

safe_mushroom.name: Exidia recisa
safe_mushroom.description: Jelly-like brownish fungus, edible when cooked.

lookalike.name: Exidia glandulosa
lookalike.description: May cause stomach upset if eaten raw.

differences: Glandulosa is black and firmer.
Recisa is amber-brown and more gelatinous.
Glandulosa sometimes confused with wood ear fungus.

safe_mushroom.name: Hygrocybe conica
safe_mushroom.description: Witch's hat, brightly colored and mildly toxic raw.

lookalike.name: Hygrocybe nigrescens
lookalike.description: Similar blackening species, may be inedible.

differences: Both blacken with age; nigrescens does so faster.
Conica more conical and waxy.
Neither is highly toxic, but may cause upset raw.

safe_mushroom.name: Inocybe erubescens
safe_mushroom.description: Rarely consumed, due to risk of confusion.

differences: White cap with lilac tint in geophylla.
Both have fibrous caps, but geophylla is smaller.
Causes salivation, sweating, and even death.
Torminosus has hairy cap edges.
Deliciosus milk is carrot-orange, torminosus is white.
Torminosus requires boiling to reduce toxicity.

safe_mushroom.name: Pluteus cervinus
safe_mushroom.description: Deer mushroom, pink gills, edible when young.

differences: Salicinus has bluish tint near gills and stem.
Cervinus has more even brown cap.
Avoid psychoactive species unless properly identified.
Emetica has bright red cap and burns tongue.
Cyanoxantha gills are flexible and cream-colored.
Taste test: emetica is very hot and bitter.

safe_mushroom.name: Suillus luteus
safe_mushroom.description: Slippery Jack, edible after skin is peeled.

lookalike.name: Suillus granulatus
lookalike.description: Less desirable; may cause GI upset raw.

differences: Granulatus lacks ring on stem unlike luteus.
Cap is thinner and more yellowish.
Slime layer more persistent on granulatus.
